messages:
incident-bot: Paging: kv-cache alert (high eviction rate + tail latency) affecting rw-hosted-us-west. Severity: P1. oncall-sre paged (emma).
oncall-sre (emma): ack — investigating. seeing KV cache evictions spike ~X10 across shard set A. continuous-batcher queue depth rising.
raj: grabbing logs, I can see a sustained stream of long-context completions mixed with many tiny embed-only requests. looks like batching fairness is favoring the long ones and starving short ones.
olivia: customer-ops — any reports from customers?
customer-ops: Received 3 support tickets in last 15m: high latency on small embedding calls, 504s for short chat completions. customers flagged increased cost due to retrying.
emma: confirming: tail p95/p99 tokens latency up ~400% on some routes. CPU on router nodes normal, but GPU queues show big imbalance. KV cache hit rate dropped from 92% -> 40% for hot prefixes.
mike: attaching quick grep of logs (abbreviated):
```
2026-03-14T02:01:12Z batch-scheduler: enq req id=abc123 size=16 seq=8
2026-03-14T02:01:12Z batch-scheduler: enq req id=def456 size=1024 seq=512
2026-03-14T02:01:12Z kv-cache: evict prefix=./chat/conv/123 count=1890
2026-03-14T02:01:12Z continuous-batcher: flush size=2048 latency=1.2s
```
emma: root cause hypothesis: a regression from last night's continuous-batching change (auto-coalesce window) that increased aggregation across request types — it inadvertently created massive mixed batches where long sessions dominate KV usage, blowing KV cache and causing frequent evictions.
raj: confirm which commit rolled yesterday? deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-14T00:40:12Z by raj — manifest: batcher: auto_coalesce=true, fairness_policy=legacy.
olivia: do we have a quick mitigation we can push? customers are getting 504s.
emma: immediate mitigations: 1) flip auto_coalesce=false 2) tighten batcher fairness config to prefer short requests (token_budget_per_batch) 3) enable aggressive KV-prefetch reduction to limit cache churn. We should do 1 & 2 first as quick config toggles.
raj: I'll stage a config patch to flip auto_coalesce=false and set fairness_policy=per_request_size. prepping canary.
mike: also propose reducing max_batch_tokens from 4096 -> 1024 for hosted tier temporarily. reduces waste and isolates long requests.
olivia: customer-ops: we should draft customer comms if we expect >30min impact.
emma: agreed. raj, mike — let's run a canary on a single router pool, prefer non-prod customer beta pool. After 5m successful, roll to prod.
raj: canary started on router-pool-7 at 02:12Z. monitoring dashboards: kv-hit-rate up slightly, eviction rate dropping.
(02:17) deploy-bot: config patch applied to router-pool-7: auto_coalesce=false, fairness=per_request_size, max_batch_tokens=1024.
emma: good signal: p95 latency down ~35% on canary; eviction rate down ~60%. proceeding to staggered roll.
customer-ops: starting proactive outreach to top affected customers, noted mitigations and ETA for full roll ~30min.
raj: rolling to remaining router pools in 3 waves. each wave ~4 pools, 3m wait.
mike: FYI, I'm preparing a hotfix branch to revert the auto-coalesce change for the next deploy and add tighter unit tests to exercise mixed-request workloads.
(02:34) raj: wave 1 -> success. wave 2 -> small blip on pool 3: one node reported kv-cache OOM and restarted; auto-rebalance recovered. No customer-facing 504s during restart.
emma: node restarted, node ops tracing shows it hit a pathological eviction loop for prefix ./chat/long/999. We'll mark that prefix for exclusion in prefetch for now.
customer-ops: we've notified affected customers that issue is mitigated and we are rolling full fix; some customers still seeing intermittent high tail latencies — escalation ongoing.
mike: hotfix branch ready: revert commit 0a7b9f -> restore batching window to previous, add fairness unit test. recommend rolling tomorrow as controlled deploy after full QA.
emma: for incident timeline & RCA prep — key factors: 1) continuous-batching auto-coalesce merged without mixed-workload regression tests 2) fairness policy didn't prioritize short requests under high long-request load 3) KV prefetch aggressiveness combined with large mixed batches caused cache blowup and evictions -> throughput collapse for short flows.
raj: immediate follow-ups: a) add mixed-workload unit + integration tests (in eng-runtime) b) add runtime guardrail: if eviction rate spikes > 3x baseline in 1m, temporarily enforce short-request priority and reduce batch size c) update runbook for oncall to include quick toggles.
olivia: customer-ops will collect ticket list and impact window, escalate to account teams where necessary.
emma: estimated customer impact window: 02:01Z -> 02:48Z (47m). we mitigated mostly by 02:20Z; residual tail spikes until 02:48Z.
customer-ops: confirming — three enterprise customers reported revenue-impacting timeouts; opened follow-ups with product & legal for credits.
(02:50) oncall-sre (emma): monitoring stable, eviction rate back to baseline, p99 within SLO. I'm going to hand off to eng-runtime for postmortem.
raj: taking ownership of action items. will schedule a hotfix rollback tomorrow and PR for guardrail improvements.
mike: I'll follow up on unit tests and add a simulation to our CI that replays mixed short/long traffic.
emma: thanks everyone. tagging postmortem thread. I'll drop initial incident notes to #postmortems and link this thread.
deploy-bot: manual rollback scheduled for 2026-03-15 03:00Z to revert auto-coalesce commit (pending approvals).
olivia: closing loop with customers: drafting email now, will include timeline and mitigation summary.
customer-ops: request: include recommended client-side retry/backoff guidance to reduce retry storms.
emma: noted — we'll add that to the message and follow with postmortem when ready.
(03:40) emma: closing incident. root cause marked as continuous-batching coalesce regression causing mixed-batch domination + KV prefetch aggressiveness -> cache churn. Follow-ups assigned. Thanks all.
